SETTINGS

1. Members of a shellfish-gathering cooperative on a tidal estuary use a species-identification and harvest-logging app to record what they collect when low tides expose the beds.

Principles: Primary: 29 (Pneumatics and hydraulics), the tidal flow determines when gathering beds are accessible, structuring the entire temporal pattern of harvesting activity. Secondary: 4 (Asymmetry), experienced gatherers reach exposed beds earlier and log first, so information flows in one direction through the society before reversing on the next tidal window.

Society: About 120 holders of gathering permits in a coastal village cooperative. They share the tidal flats, a landing point and a monthly cooperative meeting. The people a UTAUT2 survey would measure are individual permit-holding members who use the app of their own choice.

Scope: The app is a consumer identification and logging tool. No employer or contract requires it. Members choose whether and how often to use it. Use is voluntary and tied to a leisure or small-income activity.

Condition: Tidal cycles (a rhythm people do not set) determine when the beds are exposed. Experienced gatherers, attuned to tidal windows, reach the flats as the water drops and log their finds using the app's photographic species key, bed-mapping overlay and quantity-estimation tool. Those logs appear to other members and start their episodes of use. The recurrence keeps step with the experienced gatherers' attention as shaped by the tidal rhythm. Concrete episode: a spring tide exposes a rarely accessible oyster bed at 6:20 AM; an experienced gatherer photographs specimens and runs them through the species key, pins the bed on the map overlay, and estimates quantity with the counting tool; forty minutes later a less experienced member sees the log and opens the app. The pace is set by the interaction of tidal exposure and experienced gatherers' attentiveness to it.

Mechanism: Within the episode that the less experienced member's attention was drawn to, the experienced gatherer's log reveals which features of the species key, the bed-mapping overlay and the counting tool were used, and in what sequence. The social signal says two things: that one should be out gathering and logging (the social expectation, SI proper, feeding SI → BI), and that these particular features make the app useful for identifying and mapping what the beds hold (procedural guidance, the new SI → EE path). The guidance changes how easy the app seems.

Measurement: A survey of cooperative members using UTAUT2's seven-point scales, with item stems reworded for the harvest-logging app. Use is reported frequency of use on a seven-point scale. Data collection would occur at the landing point or by post.

Nearest excluded cause: "users depending on one another for the system to work." Cooperative members share the resource and coordinate some management decisions, so a form of interdependence exists in the background. The change does not rest on that interdependence. It rests on the experienced gatherer's logged use of app features starting the focal member's episode and supplying procedural guidance within it. A member who gathered on a separate bed, with no coordination, would still receive the log and the guidance it contains.

Counter-example point: This setting shows that the partial mediation of Social Influence through Effort Expectancy can arise even when the technology has no communication or messaging feature, because the social pacing enters through logged traces of tool use anchored to a shared natural environment.

Tension: The same episodes that make the app easier to learn also erode members' freedom to choose when and where to gather, because their activity becomes entrained to the pace and site choices of the most experienced gatherers.

2. Members of an astronomical society in a rural dark-sky village use an observation-logging and sky-charting app to record celestial objects on clear nights.

Principles: Primary: 39 (Inert atmosphere), the dark-sky site provides a neutral background against which each logged observation stands out as a distinct signal, so members notice and respond to individual logs rather than a stream of mixed activity. Secondary: 36 (Phase transitions), the moment a sky clears after prolonged cloud cover triggers a burst of logging by experienced observers, creating a concentrated pulse of episodes.

Society: About 90 amateur astronomers who belong to a dark-sky preservation society in a rural village. They share a ridge with observation points, a warming hut and a quarterly meeting. UTAUT2 would survey individual members who use the app of their own choice.

Scope: The app is a consumer sky-charting and logging tool used for a leisure pursuit. No one is paid or required to use it.

Condition: Celestial visibility follows atmospheric and astronomical rhythms people do not set: cloud clearance, planetary opposition, meteor-shower activity, the passage of comets. When the sky clears after a cloudy spell, experienced observers set up equipment and log detailed observations using the app's star-chart overlay, telescope-alignment wizard, eyepiece-simulation calculator and photo-stacking tool. Those logs, with timestamps, equipment parameters and feature screenshots, appear to other members and start their episodes. The recurrence keeps step with the experienced observers' attention to celestial and atmospheric rhythms. Concrete episode: a week of overcast sky breaks at 9:35 PM on the night Jupiter is near opposition; an experienced observer logs a planetary observation using the app's tracking-mount calibrator, the eyepiece-simulation tool and the detail-overlay filter; fifty minutes later a newer member sees the log and opens the same features to attempt the observation from a different spot on the ridge.

Mechanism: Within the newer member's episode, the experienced observer's log shows which app features were used and in what order: the planet-finder overlay, the eyepiece calculator with a particular focal-length setting, the tracking calibrator's drift-alignment mode. The social signal says "this is worth observing tonight" (SI proper, feeding SI → BI) and "here is how to set up the app's alignment and simulation features to see it" (procedural guidance, the new SI → EE path). The guidance changes how easy the app seems.

Measurement: A survey of society members on UTAUT2's seven-point scales, item stems reworded for the sky-charting app. Use is reported frequency of use on a seven-point scale. The survey could be administered at the warming hut or online.

Nearest excluded cause: "a calendar schedule, booked session, fixed cycle or deadline." Planetary oppositions and meteor-shower peaks have predictable calendar dates that members could mark in advance. The condition does not depend on the calendar date. It depends on the experienced observer actually going out when the sky is clear, using the app's features, and logging. A predicted shower on a cloudy night produces no logs and no episodes. The rhythm is atmospheric clarity filtered through the experienced observer's attention, not a date on a calendar.

Counter-example point: This setting shows that the partial mediation can arise when each user is observing alone and in silence, because the social pacing operates through logged feature-use rather than through co-presence, conversation or shared screen time.

Tension: The same episodes that teach newer members how to use the app's alignment and simulation features also collapse the patient, self-directed discovery that drew many members to amateur astronomy, because their observation rhythm now tracks the logging pace of experienced observers rather than their own curiosity about the sky.

3. Members of a ceramics cooperative in a village share two communal kilns and use a glaze-recipe and firing-log app to record their firings, glaze formulations, pyrometric readings and results.

Principles: Primary: 17 (Another dimension), use of the app moves off the personal screen to a shared tablet mounted on the wall of the kiln house, so that episodes of use coincide with physical visits to the kiln rather than with personal notifications on a pocket device. Secondary: 5 (Merging), the routine kiln check and the app episode are joined into a single activity at the kiln-house wall.

Society: About 70 home-based potters in a village who hold membership in a ceramics cooperative. They share the two communal kilns, a workspace for glazing, and a retail stall at a weekly market. UTAUT2 would measure individual potters who use the app voluntarily.

Scope: The app is a consumer tool for hobbyist and small-production potters. No employer requires it. Members choose whether to log their firings and consult the glaze database.

Condition: Each kiln firing is a multi-day process in which temperature rises, holds and then falls along a curve governed by the kiln's thermal mass and the fuel supply (a material process whose trajectory, once set in motion, people do not control moment to moment). Experienced potters visit the kiln during critical stages, read cones and colors, and log readings using the app's pyrometric-cone calculator, glaze-chemistry display and before-and-after photo overlay. Those logs remain on the shared tablet and start episodes for other potters who come to the kiln next. The recurrence follows the experienced potters' attention to the kiln's thermal stages: they check when the kiln demands it, at intervals set by the pace of heat-work accumulation. Concrete episode: during a reduction stoneware firing, an experienced potter checks the kiln as cone 9 begins to bend, logs the cone angle using the calculator, photographs the spy-hole view and annotates it with the glaze-chemistry overlay showing predicted melt behavior; three hours later another potter arrives for the next check, sees the log on the tablet, and opens the same features.

Mechanism: Within the second potter's episode, the first potter's log shows which features were used: the cone-calculator's angle-entry mode, the glaze-chemistry overlay's expansion coefficients, the photo tool's comparison slider. The social signal says "the firing needs monitoring, you should check it" (SI proper, feeding SI → BI) and "here is how to use the measurement and chemistry features to read what the kiln is doing" (procedural guidance, the new SI → EE path). The guidance changes how easy the app seems.

Measurement: A survey of cooperative members on UTAUT2's seven-point scales, item stems reworded for the firing-log app. Use is reported frequency of use on a seven-point scale. The survey could be administered at the kiln house or the market stall.

Nearest excluded cause: "users depending on one another for the system to work." Cooperative members share the kiln, and one potter's firing decisions affect another's pieces in the same load. The change does not rest on this shared-load interdependence. It rests on the experienced potter's logged use of app features starting the next potter's episode and supplying procedural guidance within it. A potter who had no pieces in the current load would still encounter the log when visiting the kiln house and still receive the guidance.

Counter-example point: This setting shows that the partial mediation can operate through a shared physical location and a wall-mounted device, without any digital notification reaching a personal screen, because the spatial arrangement forces episodes to coincide with traces of other users' feature-use.

Tension: The same episodes that teach potters how to use the app's pyrometric and glaze-chemistry features also compress each potter's individual sense of when a firing is right, because the logged reading from an experienced potter's episode becomes the benchmark the next potter measures against rather than developing a feel for the kiln.

4. Members of a beekeeping association on an island use a hive-monitoring app that reads sensor data (temperature, weight, acoustic spectrum) from their hives and allows them to log observations and management decisions.

Principles: Primary: 24 (Intermediary), the bees' foraging and brood rhythms act as an intermediary between the island's bloom patterns and the beekeeper's attention, so that the rhythm pacing episodes of app use passes through a living system that neither the keeper nor the island's ecology fully controls. Secondary: 3 (Local quality), each apiary's microclimate and colony genetics produce slightly different rhythmic signatures, so the practice varies from site to site within the same small island.

Society: About 80 amateur and small-scale beekeepers on an island who belong to a beekeeping association. They share forage zones, coordinate seasonal mite treatments, and meet at the association hall and at a honey market. UTAUT2 would measure individual beekeepers who use the app voluntarily.

Scope: The app is a consumer hive-monitoring tool. No employer or contract requires its use. Members keep bees as a hobby or modest sideline.

Condition: Bee colonies follow foraging rhythms tied to bloom cycles and weather, rhythms people do not set. When nectar flow begins, hive weight rises and acoustic patterns shift. Experienced beekeepers notice these sensor changes and log detailed observations using the app's weight-trend graph, acoustic-analysis spectrogram, queen-status estimator and swarm-risk algorithm. Those logs start episodes for other beekeepers who receive them. The recurrence follows the bees' foraging rhythm as filtered through the experienced keepers' attention. Concrete episode: a spring bloom begins on the island's western cliffs and hive weight rises 1.4 kg in a morning; an experienced keeper opens the weight-trend graph, annotates the slope, runs the acoustic spectrogram to check for queen piping, queries the swarm-risk algorithm, and logs all of it with a photograph of the flight board; ninety minutes later a newer keeper on the eastern side of the island sees the log and opens the same features on her own hive's data.

Mechanism: Within the newer keeper's episode, the experienced keeper's log shows which features were used: the weight-trend annotation tool, the spectrogram's frequency-band filter, the swarm-risk algorithm's input screen. The social signal says "your colonies may be responding to the same flow, check them" (SI proper, feeding SI → BI) and "here is how to read weight slopes, filter acoustic data and query the swarm-risk model in the app" (procedural guidance, the new SI → EE path). The guidance changes how easy the app seems.

Measurement: A survey of association members on UTAUT2's seven-point scales, item stems reworded for the hive-monitoring app. Use is reported frequency of use on a seven-point scale. The survey could be administered at the association hall or the honey market.

Nearest excluded cause: "a season or another rhythm that people do not set may pace other users' activity under rule 5, but may not itself start the focal person's episodes." The spring bloom is seasonal, and one might argue that the bloom itself starts the focal person's episode. It does not. The bloom triggers the bees' foraging, which changes the sensor data, which prompts the experienced keeper to log, and the experienced keeper's log starts the focal person's episode. The bloom acts through the bees and through the experienced keeper's attention, not on the focal person directly.

Counter-example point: This setting shows that the partial mediation can arise when the technology monitors a non-human biological system rather than human activity, because the rhythm that paces social influence passes through an organism whose behavior neither user controls.

Tension: The same episodes that teach newer keepers how to use the app's diagnostic features also make their management decisions track the experienced keeper's interpretive frame rather than their own colony's particular signals, because the procedural guidance arrives before the newer keeper has formed an independent reading of the data.

5. Members of a freshwater aquarist society in a town use a water-quality testing and tank-management app to log chemical parameters, dosing calculations, livestock observations and equipment maintenance for their home aquaria.

Principles: Primary: 7 (Nested doll), an aquarium is a contained ecosystem nested within a household, nested within the society of keepers, and the monitoring practice propagates from the innermost biological rhythm outward through each enclosing layer, so that a bacterial event inside a glass box on one member's shelf eventually starts an episode on another member's phone across town. Secondary: 32 (Colour changes), visible shifts in the tank (algae tint, water cloudiness, shrimp coloration after a molt) act as biological signals that prompt the experienced keeper to test and log.

Society: About 110 hobbyist fishkeepers in a town who belong to an aquarist society. They share a bulk-supply order, a monthly swap meeting and an online group hosted on the society's own page. UTAUT2 would measure individual members who use the app voluntarily.

Scope: The app is a consumer tool for hobbyist fishkeeping. No one is paid or required to use it. Members keep aquaria for personal interest.

Condition: Biological cycles in a planted freshwater aquarium (bacterial blooms in filter media, algae growth spurts triggered by nutrient imbalance, shrimp molting tied to water-change frequency, plant pearling after a large water change) follow rhythms set by the organisms and the tank's chemistry, not by the keeper. When a cycle event occurs, experienced keepers test water parameters and log the results using the app's parameter-entry screen, trend-comparison graph, dosing calculator and photo-journal. Those logs start episodes for other members. The recurrence follows the biological rhythms of each tank as filtered through the experienced keeper's attention. Concrete episode: a bacterial bloom clouds an experienced keeper's tank three days after a filter cleaning; the keeper measures ammonia, nitrite and nitrate with test kits and enters results on the app's parameter screen, compares the values to the preceding week on the trend graph, adjusts fertiliser dosing with the calculator's dilution formula, and logs a photo-journal entry showing the cloudiness; later that day, two other members see the log and open the same features to check their own tanks' readings.

Mechanism: Within the other members' episodes, the experienced keeper's log shows which features were used and how: the parameter-entry interface's dropdown for test-kit brand, the trend graph's week-over-week comparison mode, the dosing calculator's dilution formula with specific input fields. The social signal says "your tank could face the same problem, check it" (SI proper, feeding SI → BI) and "here is how to enter test results, read the trend comparison and run the dosing formula in the app" (procedural guidance, the new SI → EE path). The guidance changes how easy the app seems.

Measurement: A survey of society members on UTAUT2's seven-point scales, item stems reworded for the tank-management app. Use is reported frequency of use on a seven-point scale. The survey could be administered at the monthly swap or by post.

Nearest excluded cause: "trust in other users." Hobbyist fishkeepers often defer to experienced members' water-chemistry knowledge, and trust in a veteran keeper's parameter readings could drive app adoption independently of C. The change does not rest on trust in the experienced keeper's interpretation of the readings. It rests on the procedural guidance embedded in the way the experienced keeper navigated the app's features within the logged episode. A member who disagreed with the experienced keeper's diagnosis would still gain guidance on how to use the parameter-entry screen, the trend graph's comparison mode and the dosing calculator.

Counter-example point: This setting shows that the partial mediation arises even when each user's monitored system is physically sealed off from every other user's, because the social pacing operates entirely through logged episodes of feature-use rather than through any shared environment, co-located activity or mutual observation.

Tension: The same episodes that teach members how to use the app's testing and dosing features also flatten the individuality of each aquarium's ecology, because the procedural guidance arrives packaged with a particular diagnostic protocol that may not suit a tank with different livestock, plant load or source-water chemistry.
